rationale: Operator, 2026-11-07, decision rubric run by the planner. The 30-minute heartbeat age is a scheduler-side proxy: the stamp is written only at step transitions, so a developer round longer than 30 minutes is indistinguishable from a dead executor (AISDLC-1209 reaped mid-round 2026-11-06T19:45Z; AISDLC-948 and AISDLC-1124 were earlier patches to the same proxy). Comparable systems (Temporal activity heartbeats, GitHub Actions runner-disconnect plus per-step timeout, Kubernetes holder-renewed leases) let the holder own its liveness and budget; none reap on elapsed time since the last step. Counter-argument considered: an executor-published busy state is itself a proxy and a hung subagent reports busy forever. Rebuttal: the step-owned budget (AISDLC-1219) catches that case and ends the round as iterate-needed keeping the worktree, never a restart from zero; pane death (AISDLC-1217) catches the crash case. Rejected patch-proxy (keeps the age number and retry-from-zero, which were never requirements of AISDLC-826) and status-quo (planner refreshes heartbeats by hand). Implementation: AISDLC-1216 to 1219; RFC-0041 OQ-3 and the RFC-0051 stall paragraph get an amendment note, no Resolution marker.
